fact_rationales.F12: Low hemoglobin is consistent with anemia, which can be seen in acute lymphoblastic leukemia due to bone marrow infiltration.
fact_rationales.F14: Elevated leukocyte count with 35% blasts is highly suggestive of acute leukemia, and the presence of blasts is more characteristic of acute lymphoblastic leukemia than other types of leukemia.

why.B1.1: High leukocyte count with 35% blasts and anemia are more characteristic of Acute Myeloid Leukemia
why.B2.1: Elevated leukocyte count with 35% blasts is also consistent with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia, but less specific than the findings for Acute Myeloid Leukemia

ranked_facts.why: high leukocyte count with 35% blasts is strongly indicative of acute leukemia
anemia is common in various myeloid neoplasms

fact_rationales.F12: Anemia (Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL) is more common in Acute Myeloid Leukemia than in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia in Blast Crisis, but can be seen in Myelodysplastic Syndrome with Excess Blasts.
fact_rationales.F14: A high leukocyte count with 35% blasts is highly suggestive of Acute Myeloid Leukemia, and can also be seen in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia in Blast Crisis, but is less common in Myelodysplastic Syndrome with Excess Blasts.
